Agpool is a set of zero-knowledge privacy pools on EVM chains. You shield funds into a pool, then send, swap or bridge them without any on-chain link between the money that went in and the money that comes out. Nothing is held for you: every balance is a note only your wallet can spend.

Agpool is open-source software: zero-knowledge privacy pool contracts deployed on public blockchains, plus a website, app, relayer API and CLI that help you use them. Agpool is not a bank, broker, exchange, money transmitter or custodian, and it does not hold your funds. Pool balances are notes that only your keys can spend.
Agpool never asks for your recovery phrase or private key, and never messages you first.
Agpool works the same without the token; every fee is paid in the asset you move.

agpool.cash is a static site served through Cloudflare. It sets no cookies, loads no analytics or advertising scripts and keeps no account data in browser storage: your sign-in signature lives in memory and is gone when you close the tab. Your browser talks directly to public RPC endpoints of each chain (Robinhood Chain, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain) to read balances and confirm transactions; those providers see your IP address and the public addresses being queried.
AI agents can find Agpool by name in the official MCP Registry and on Glama, where both the local server and the hosted endpoint are verified listings.

Your device derives your keys from the sign-in signature, finds your notes in public pool data and generates every proof (the web app in a background worker, the CLI in Node). The relayer receives only the finished proof and its public inputs, so it cannot spend, redirect or resize your payment: changing any field invalidates the proof. What the relayer can do is refuse or delay a relay, and like any server it sees your IP address and the public data of the transactions it broadcasts. Pool data comes from our indexer; your device rebuilds the Merkle tree from it and the contract only accepts proofs against roots it has seen, so stale or wrong data makes a transaction fail rather than misdirect funds.

Your IP address is used for rate limiting in memory (a one-minute window). Our hosting providers (Cloudflare and Railway) keep standard request logs — time, path, status, IP address — for a limited period under their own policies.
